metadata.case_name: WONG CHI WING v. WONG TAK WAI AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: semiskilled worker in the electro-elating trade
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: good prospects of re-employment in the electro-elating field after the Chinese New Year holiday

injuries.description: Admitted to Queen Elizabeth Hospital on 29th January 1984 with serious injuries and concussion. Plaintiff suffered several hours of post-traumatic amnesia but has had no post concussional symptoms.
source:
(1)

Admitted to Queen Elizabeth Hospital on 29th January 1984 with serious
injuries and concussion. Plaintiff suffered several hours of post-traumatic
amnesia but has had no post concussional symptoms.

injuries.description: Several lacerations including a scar across the bridge of his nose and on the right upper lip.
injuries.body_part: bridge of nose; right upper lip
source:
(2)

Plaintiff suffered several lacerations including a scar across the bridge of
his nose and on the right upper lip. These scars are not noticeable and have
not altered the shape of the face.

injuries.description: A fractured right upper jaw and cheek bone with five teeth in the lower jaw damaged; the four incisor teeth and the right canine were removed and replaced with a denture.
injuries.body_part: right upper jaw and cheek bone; lower jaw teeth
source:
(3)

A fractured right upper jaw and cheek bone but there is no displacement and it
has healed perfectly. Five teeth in the lower jaw were damaged and the four
incisor teeth and the right canine were removed and replaced with by a
denture.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures involving skull or facial bones

injuries.description: A ruptured spleen and right diaphragm. The spleen was removed and the tear in the diaphragm repaired; a drain inserted in the chest was removed after 5 days when the lung re-expanded.
source:
(4)

A ruptured spleen and right diaphragm. The spleen was removed on operation and
the tear in the diaphragm repaired. A drain inserted in the chest was removed
after 5 days when the lung re-expanded.

injuries.description: Fracture of the pelvis and a disruption of the pubic bones requiring fixation by a bone plate and bone screws (which were removed a few days before leaving hospital).
source:
(5)

The most serious injury was the fracture of the pelvis and a disruption of the
pubic bones. The position of the pubic bones was secured by a bone plate and
bone screws which were removed a few days before leaving hospital.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of pubis without disruption of pelvic ring

injuries.description: A rupture of the bladder and the urethra which were repaired on operation; a catheter was inserted to drain the bladder. This has left Plaintiff with considerable difficulty in passing urine and he will require periodic dilitation treatment in hospital to empty his bladder for the remainder of his life.
source:
(6)

A rupture of the bladder and the urethra which were repaired on operation when
a catheter was inserted through the penis to drain the bladder. This has left
Plaintiff with a considerable difficulty in passing urine and he will require
periodic dilitation treatment in hospital to empty his bladder for the
remainder of his life.

manifestations.description: scars across the bridge of his nose and on the right upper lip (not noticeable and have not altered the shape of the face)
four incisor teeth and the right canine were removed and replaced with a denture
considerable difficulty in passing urine and will require periodic dilitation treatment in hospital to empty his bladder for the remainder of his life
permanent difficulty lifting heavy weights; restricted to light work during his working life; earning capacity reduced by 20%
real risk of bladder infection which could spread to his kidney and may reduce life expectancy by 10%
a slight pain on the left side of his pelvis when he sits for a lengthy period or when he squats or bends his body
a dull pain in his bladder

treatments_received: The spleen was removed on operation
the tear in the diaphragm repaired
a drain inserted in the chest was removed after 5 days when the lung re-expanded
the position of the pubic bones was secured by a bone plate and bone screws (removed a few days before leaving hospital)
the bladder and the urethra were repaired on operation
a catheter was inserted through the penis to drain the bladder
periodic dilitation treatment in hospital to empty his bladder for the remainder of his life
treatments_future: periodic dilitation treatment in hospital to empty his bladder for the remainder of his life

losses.description: A scar on his chest causes him embarrassment and he does not swim now.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He engaged in outdoor activities such as swimming and running before the accident but said he did not swim now because a scar on his chest causes him embarrassment.
Considerable difficulty in passing urine and requirement for periodic dilitation treatment in hospital for the remainder of his life.
Restricted to light work during his working life and his earning capacity reduced by 20%.
Plaintiff's life expectancy would be reduced by 10%.
